children: is nearing an agreement to sell 150 737 Max jets to Turkish Airlines after a dispute over engine maintenance delayed the order, Reuters reported Tuesday, citing people familiar with the negotiations.
The purchase is part of a broader agreement for 225 Boeing
aircraft announced after Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan met U.S. President Donald Trump last year. The Max portion could be finalized as soon as next week.

Turkish Airlines had threatened to switch the order to Airbus amid disagreements with engine manufacturer CFM International over maintenance costs, spare-parts prices and long-term repair risks. CFM is jointly owned by GE Aerospace

The carrier also sought a leading role in CFM’s maintenance network, which would give it faster access to repair technology for engines used on the 737 Max. It remains unclear whether that request will be included in the final agreement.

A completed order would preserve one of the major Boeing agreements announced by the White House last year. Turkish media have reported that Trump and Erdogan may meet during United Nations gatherings in New York next week.

Turkish Airlines operates more than 400 Boeing and Airbus aircraft. It is also considering regional jets from Embraer and Airbus as well as the larger Boeing 777X and Airbus A350-1000 as it expands its Istanbul hub.

title: Boeing is said to near deal with Turkish Airlines for 150 737 Max jets
